idiom_name: class per table with classmethod find and instance insert/update over DB-API (sqlite3/psycopg) placeholders
implementation_notes: Python's DB-API gives cursors, tuples and a row factory - not row objects - so the gateway is a plain class whose attributes mirror the columns, a classmethod (or module-level function) that runs a parameterised SELECT and constructs the instance, and insert/update/delete methods that execute against a connection passed in by the caller. sqlite3.Row (or psycopg's dict_row) removes positional indexing but adds no persistence behaviour; SQLAlchemy's ORM provides a different pattern (Active Record or Data Mapper), so the classic structure stays hand-written when you want it.
pitfalls: sqlite3 connections are bound to their creating thread (check_same_thread) and are not safe to share across threads without serialisation.
DB-API transactions are implicit: without an explicit commit/rollback discipline (or autocommit) a 'successful' insert can be rolled back when the connection closes.
The SELECT column order is part of the contract when constructing from a plain tuple; keep the order and the constructor in sync or use a row factory.
Binding a datetime/Decimal without an adapter silently stores a string; register adapters or convert explicitly.
